meta.title: Politics: The Daily Signal, Election Results & Accountability

daily.standfirst: The developments worth following, the evidence behind them and the questions still open.

daily.five_intro: The November 5 briefing in five questions. Each opens the full reporting, with what we know, what remains open and what we report next.

accountability.h2: A new majority. The same leaders?
accountability.deck: Hakeem Jeffries is seeking the speakership. Chuck Schumer expects to become Senate majority leader. Their colleagues will decide whether to keep the party's current leadership or chart another course.
accountability.no_data: We're collecting attributable public positions and verifying the source of each one. An unanswered request is not a vote or a position.

election.h2: The election is over. The record isn't.
election.deck: Explore the results, campaign money and reporting that shaped the contests. Each state report brings the vote counts together with what changed and what comes next.

money.deck: Campaign filings and outside spending show who tried to influence the election. Follow the disclosures, the beneficiaries and the limits of what those records can establish.

record.deck: Campaign positions are part of the public record. Now we follow the votes, appointments and decisions that show what happens after Election Day.

signals.h2: What the numbers reveal — and what they don't.
signals.deck: Margins, turnout, geography and spending can reveal important patterns. We show the comparisons, the sources and the uncertainty behind each finding.
signals.no_signal: No finding has passed our review yet. Until one does, we publish none.
